problem: The sentence "If ρ t is negative and the sphere rises" is garbled and states no condition. Read literally it is meaningless, and the student cannot tell when the ball rises.
fix: If ρ < σ, the terminal speed v_t comes out negative and the sphere rises instead of falling (upthrust exceeds weight).

problem: The viscosity of glycerine is quoted as ≈ 0.8 Pa·s with no temperature, while water is correctly tied to 20 °C. Glycerine's η changes steeply with temperature: about 1.4 Pa·s at 20 °C and about 0.8 Pa·s only near 27–30 °C, so a student may memorize 0.8 Pa·s as the 20 °C value.
fix: State the temperature: glycerine ≈ 1.4 Pa·s near 20 °C, falling to ≈ 0.8 Pa·s near 27–30 °C. Say the worked example uses 0.83 Pa·s, i.e. glycerine at about 27 °C.

problem: The plotted curve 6.9(1 − e^(−2t)) has a time constant of 0.5 s, so the ball takes about 2 s to reach terminal speed. For the 2 mm steel ball of the worked example the real time constant is a few milliseconds, so the figure's time axis is not physical.
fix: Label the figure as a sketch of the shape of the curve (speed rising and levelling at the terminal value) and say the real approach time for a 2 mm ball is only a few milliseconds.
